newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's "pirate of the airwaves" interrupts again.
newsitem.headline: Italy's "pirate of the airwaves" interrupts again.

text.p: Italy's so-called "pirate of the airwaves", who interrupts television programmes to broadcast messages supporting separatism for northern Italy, struck again on Tuesday.

Officials said the the latest incident, in which the voice of an unknown man with a Venice accent cut into a news programme, occurred a week before the 200th anniversary on May 12 of the fall of the Venetian republic.

Similar interruptions have happened at least five times in recent months. On one occasion a man speaking in a thick Venetian accent drowned out the voice of Scarlett O'Hara, the heroine of the movie "Gone with the Wind".
Recently, the voice has urged northerners to gather for a mass rally in Venice on May 12.
The separatist Northern League party, which proclaimed independence for its self-styled state of Padania in Venice last year, has denied involvement.
Venice, known as the "Serenissima" or "Most Serene", was a republic for 14 centuries but lost its independence in 1797 when the French took control.
